Why this project

A better view of the women who train.

Strength training is often discussed through elite athletes, before-and-after photos, or generic fitness advice. This project starts somewhere quieter: with a nationally representative public-health survey and questions that leave room for complexity.

01

Measure participation

How often do women report doing activities designed to strengthen their muscles?

02

Look past a single metric

Compare training frequency with measured grip strength and body-composition variables.

03

Keep the caveats visible

Show what the survey can tell us—and what it cannot say about programs, gyms, or causation.

The data plan

One survey. Five lenses.

We are starting with one NHANES cycle so the first release stays understandable, reproducible, and honest. The site can expand to additional cycles after the foundation is sound.

PAQ_G · PAD440 / PAD460

Muscle-strengthening activity

Whether a participant did muscle-strengthening activities in the past 30 days, plus reported frequency.

◌

MGX_G

Measured grip strength

A physical measurement that gives the analysis a real-world strength signal.

◐

DXX_G

Body composition

Whole-body DXA measurements for a more careful view than BMI alone.

DSQIDS_G · DSQTOT_G

Dietary supplements

Reported supplement use and nutrient totals, creating an optional bridge to the project’s original FDA direction.

Methods, in plain language

What this project will—and will not—claim.

NHANES can help us study patterns among women who report strength-training activity. It cannot identify bodybuilding programs, specific gyms, training quality, or the full lived experience of women who lift.

Population

The analysis will focus on adult female participants as coded by the source dataset. We will preserve the dataset’s own demographic definitions rather than inventing new ones.

Association, not causation

A relationship between training frequency and another measure does not prove that one caused the other. Survey weights and design variables will be used where appropriate.

Privacy by default

This project uses public, de-identified data. It will not collect names, gym locations, contact details, or personal training logs.
